story: Waymo brings cold-weather self-driving testing to Alaska, with its cars seen in Fairbanks

repeat_reasons.reason: first response was a summary; targeted repeat for verbatim quotes
first response paraphrased; targeted repeat for exact excerpts
first response gave a fragment of the Dunleavy quote
first response was a summary with no verbatim text

claims.claim: Waymo published a blog post on November 5th about how the Waymo Driver handles severe winter weather.
claims.verbatim: How the Waymo Driver Manages Severe Winter Weather
claims.notes: Byline The Waymo Team, dated November 5, 2026.

claims.claim: Waymo said that this season in Alaska it will conduct closed-course evaluations and collect data in heavy snowfall.
claims.verbatim: This season in Alaska, for example, we'll be conducting closed-course evaluations and heavy snowfall data collection.
claims.notes: Waymo's post names Alaska, not Fairbanks. Fairbanks is sourced to C08, C17, C19.

claims.claim: Waymo says it has driven tens of thousands of real-world miles in Upstate New York, Michigan's Upper Peninsula and the Sierra Nevada.
claims.value: tens of thousands of real-world miles
claims.verbatim: tens of thousands of real-world miles across Upstate New York, Michigan's Upper Peninsula and the Sierra Nevada
claims.notes: Self-reported; phrase as Waymo says.

claims.claim: The 6th-generation Waymo Driver uses cameras, radar and lidar.
claims.verbatim: The 6th-generation Waymo Driver uses cameras, radar, and lidar
claims.notes: Alaska's News Source and FOX Weather also name the sixth-generation Driver.

claims.claim: Waymo says built-in heaters and micro-wipers keep its sensors clear in icy conditions.
claims.verbatim: built-in heaters and micro-wipers keep sensors clear in icy conditions.
claims.notes: FOX Weather paraphrases the same point.

claims.claim: Waymo says it is equipping its winter vehicles with snow tires and measuring traction changes under each wheel in real time.
claims.verbatim: it measures real-time traction changes under each wheel
claims.notes: Second excerpt: we're equipping our vehicles with snow tires.

claims.claim: Waymo says that when weather exceeds what it has validated it may reduce its service area or pause service entirely.
claims.verbatim: including reducing the service area or pausing our service entirely
claims.notes: The hours or days wording was not captured; do not use it.

claims.claim: Waymo vehicles were spotted in Fairbanks after a Facebook post appeared to show them charging at electric vehicle ports in the Golden Valley Electric Association parking lot.
claims.verbatim: a post on the Fairbanks, Alaska Facebook page claiming to show them charging at electric vehicle ports
claims.notes: Byline Alex Bengel; published November 10th though the URL path says the 11th.

claims.claim: GVEA's Ashley Bradish confirmed she had personally seen the Waymo vehicles using the co-op's charging stations.
claims.verbatim: confirmed that she has personally seen the vehicles using their stations
claims.notes: Bradish also said several companies test equipment in Fairbanks cold (paraphrase only).

claims.claim: Waymo told Alaska's News Source that the work includes manual data collection, autonomous driving with a specialist at the wheel, and limited structured testing.
claims.verbatim: manual data collection, autonomous driving with a specialist at the wheel
claims.notes: Limited structured testing captured in summary only; quote only the first two modes verbatim.

claims.claim: Waymo spokesperson Chris Bonelli said the testing will help the company refine critical cold-weather capabilities.
claims.verbatim: This will allow us to further refine critical cold-weather capabilities
claims.notes: Quote no further than this excerpt.

claims.claim: As of Alaska's News Source's report, Bonelli had not answered its follow-up questions, including the testing timeline, why Waymo chose Fairbanks and whether it plans driverless cars there.
claims.verbatim: Bonelli has not yet responded to a series of questions from Alaska's News Source
claims.notes: The three topics come from the same page's summary. Soften as of the report.

claims.claim: Fairbanks Mayor Mindy O'Neall said the testing is a great opportunity for Fairbanks to be a testing ground.
claims.verbatim: I think it's a great opportunity for Fairbanks to be a testing ground.
claims.notes: Typographic apostrophe normalized.

claims.claim: Fairbanks resident Katrina Howe told Alaska's News Source that computers are actually quite stupid.
claims.verbatim: computers are actually quite stupid
claims.notes: Fragment of a longer quote; use as a quoted fragment, paired with the mayor.

claims.claim: Fairbanks resident Gwen Jackson said she expects the cars will probably just stall out.
claims.verbatim: I feel like they'll probably just stall out
claims.notes: Residents' concerns per summary: black ice, fog on sensors, cold battery failures, stalled cars.

claims.claim: Fairbanks resident Charlie Woolwine said he does not think the cars are safe and that they should not be allowed.
claims.verbatim: I don't think that they're safe and they shouldn't be allowed.
claims.notes: Apostrophes normalized.

claims.claim: Governor Mike Dunleavy said there is no better proving ground for winter driving than Fairbanks.
claims.verbatim: there is no better proving ground for winter driving than Fairbanks
claims.notes: Byline Kieran Sullivan. Full quote opens 'Alaska has always been a place where innovators come to test their limits'; quote fragments separately.

claims.claim: According to FOX Weather, Dunleavy said Waymo will test its Ojai and Hyundai IONIQ vehicles in Fairbanks.
claims.verbatim: Waymo will test its Ojai and Hyundai IONIQ vehicles in Fairbanks
claims.notes: Attribute to the governor via FOX Weather.

claims.claim: FOX Weather reported that Waymo will test its autonomous vehicles in Fairbanks during the winter.
claims.verbatim: Waymo will test its autonomous vehicles in Fairbanks, Alaska, during the winter.
claims.notes: Photo caption; corroborated by C08 and C09.

claims.claim: Fairbanks had 6 hours and 29 minutes of daylight on November 13th, with sunrise at 9.20 a.m. and sunset at 3.49 p.m.
claims.verbatim: 9:20 am - 3:49 pm  6 hours, 29 minutes
claims.notes: Background for the art. Table length 6:28:41, change minus 6:34 per day.

claims.claim: Golden Valley Electric Association's energy emergency page showed Level 0, normal operations, as of its October 24th posting.
claims.verbatim: LEVEL 0 - Normal Operations
claims.notes: Background only; timestamp October 24, 2026, 7:00 p.m.

claims.claim: The Fairbanks North Star Borough Planning Commission unanimously recommended approval of a moratorium on large-scale commercial data centers.
claims.verbatim: unanimously recommended approval of an ordinance Tuesday to place a moratorium on large-scale commercial data centers
claims.notes: Byline Jack Barnwell. Tuesday is November 10th per C28. No vote count given.

claims.claim: The commission recommended extending the moratorium to 18 months from the 12 months the borough administration requested.
claims.verbatim: expanding that moratorium to 18 months, instead of the 12 months requested by the borough administration

claims.claim: Spillman said five megawatts, the moratorium's power threshold, is enough to power at least 3,000 homes.
claims.verbatim: Five megawatts is enough to power at least 3,000 homes, Spillman said.
claims.notes: Estimate; attribute.

claims.claim: The moratorium covers data centers occupying at least 40,000 square feet of gross floor space.
claims.verbatim: occupy at least 40,000 square feet of gross floor space
claims.notes: NAEC says the draft said 50,000 and staff recommended 40,000.

claims.claim: General Use-1 zoning, where a commercial data center could technically be built, applies to 97 percent of the borough.
claims.verbatim: The GU-1 zoning applies to 97% of the borough.

claims.claim: Military land outside the fence line at installations such as Eielson is subject to borough zoning powers.
claims.verbatim: military land outside the fence line is subject to borough zoning powers
claims.notes: Does not name the enhanced use lease.

claims.claim: The Northern Alaska Environmental Center said the Planning Commission would take up Ordinance 2026-42 on Tuesday, November 10th, at 6 p.m.
claims.verbatim: a proposal to temporarily suspend land use permits for large-scale data centers
claims.notes: Advocacy notice; number and date from the same response.

claims.claim: The commission's amendment requires the planning department to report back in 10 months with its findings.
claims.verbatim: require the planning department to report back in 10 months with its findings
claims.notes: Disputed within source (also says six months); leave out of the deck.

claims.claim: The ordinance now goes to the Borough Assembly for a public hearing and approval.
claims.verbatim: The ordinance will go to the Assembly for public hearing and approval.
claims.notes: No hearing date given.

claims.claim: The University of Alaska Board of Regents delayed its statement of intent on AI use at its November meeting.
claims.verbatim: UA regents delay statement of intent on AI amid feedback
claims.notes: Byline Alex Bengel. Action on Friday, November 6th. Document is the draft AI Engaged.

claims.claim: The regents pushed the final decision to February, or sooner if UA President Matt Cooper requests it.
claims.verbatim: The final decision is pushed to February, or until UA President Matt Cooper requests it sooner.
claims.notes: Primary board site returned 503.

claims.claim: Jonathon Taylor of the UA system said the board had received a lot of feedback from a variety of stakeholders across the system.
claims.verbatim: We've received a lot of feedback from a variety of stakeholders across the system.
claims.notes: Do not print a title.
